stem: An 8-year-old child with a very restrictive diet develops progressive spastic paraparesis; which potentially vitamin-responsive cause should be considered?
explanation: Vitamin B12 deficiency is the best answer because restrictive diets can cause reversible nutritional neurological disease, and B12 deficiency is a recognised cause of progressive spastic paraparesis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: What Not to Miss in Neurology

optionExplanations.A: Correct because vitamin B12 deficiency can cause progressive spastic paraparesis and should be considered in a child with a restrictive diet.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because vitamin C deficiency does not fit the classic vitamin-responsive neurological cause of spastic paraparesis here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because vitamin K deficiency is associated with bleeding problems rather than this neurological presentation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because zinc deficiency is not the key vitamin-responsive explanation for progressive spastic paraparesis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because vitamin A deficiency is not the recognised cause of this neurological syndrome.
